Hostinger review 2026: Is this budget-friendly host still a top pick for developers, bloggers, and small businesses? In this updated look, we dive into pricing, performance, features, and real‑world usability to help you decide if Hostinger fits your software‑focused projects in 2026.

## Overview
### What is Hostinger?
Hostinger is a web hosting provider known for low‑cost plans, a custom control panel called hPanel, and a suite of tools aimed at beginners and tech‑savvy users alike. Over the years it has expanded from shared hosting to cloud, VPS, and even specialized WordPress packages.

### Why 2026 Review?
The hosting landscape shifts quickly—new hardware, security threats, and customer expectations evolve each year. A 2026 review lets us see how Hostinger’s infrastructure, support, and feature set have adapted to the latest demands, especially for software developers who need reliable environments for testing and deployment.

## Pricing Plans
### Shared Hosting
Hostinger’s shared tiers start at roughly $1.99 / month for the Single plan, $2.99 / month for Premium, and $3.99 / month for Business. All include a free SSL certificate, weekly backups (on higher tiers), and access to the hPanel. Renewal rates rise after the initial term, but the introductory pricing remains among the lowest in the industry.

### Cloud Hosting
Cloud plans begin around $7.99 / month, offering dedicated resources, a dedicated IP, and easier scaling. These are ideal for growing SaaS projects or sites that experience traffic spikes. The cloud layer runs on Google Cloud and Amazon AWS infrastructure, giving solid performance benchmarks.

### VPS Hosting
VPS options start at $3.99 / month for a basic 1 CPU, 2 GB RAM setup and scale up to $77.99 / month for higher‑end configurations. Full root access, choice of OS (Linux distributions), and SSD storage make these plans attractive for developers who need a sandbox for custom software or containerized apps.
